text: Digital anomaly: Library catalog system spontaneously generates call numbers for books that were never written. Patrons successfully check out these nonexistent volumes. Return dates are always yesterday.

Botanical survey 1891: Specimen of Quercus temporalis collected in Yorkshire. Tree rings indicate 400 years of growth completed in single afternoon. Acorns germinate into fully mature oaks instantaneously upon planting.
Census data from the Great Mice Revolution of 1603 lists seventeen human casualties and 40,000 rodent knights. The revolution succeeded. No subsequent records explain why we remember it differently.

Marginalia discovered in 14th century psalter: The cathedral dreams of flying south for winter. Architectural survey confirms NotreDame de Paris shifts 3.2 degrees southward each October, returns by spring.

Meteorological report, Antarctic research station, July 1987: Blizzard deposited snow that fell upward when disturbed. Samples contained pollen from flowers that bloom only in perpetual darkness. No such flowers exist.

Archaeological survey, Mesopotamia, 2400 BCE site: Recovered USB drive with cuneiform adapter. Contains administrative records for ziggurats not yet constructed. Files are readonly, modification date shows 2156 BCE.

Personal diary, London, 1666: Woman records attending her own funeral, taking detailed notes on eulogy accuracy. Burial register confirms death occurred. Marriage certificate shows she wed the gravedigger three months later.

Crossreference anomaly: Magna Carta signed 1215 contains clause about digital privacy rights. Parchment authentic, ink periodcorrect. Clause written in Middle English that won't develop for 200 years.

Dental records from Pompeii victim show orthodontic work completed in 1987. Victim died 79 CE. Brackets are titanium alloy, wisdom teeth removed with laser precision. No anachronistic materials found elsewhere in remains.

Botanical survey, Amazon basin, 1953: Documented tree species that photosynthesizes moonlight exclusively. Samples collected during lunar eclipse remained metabolically active. Species not found in any taxonomic database.

Archaeological report: Pleistocene site, 18,000 BCE, mammoth bones arranged in perfect fibonacci spiral. Pattern requires mathematical knowledge predating agriculture by 8,000 years. Arrangement appears deliberate, not scavenger activity.

Structural engineering report, Tower Bridge 1894: Bridge calculates its own stress loads. Blueprints contain handwritten notes in Victorian cursive predicting traffic patterns through 2089. Notes are 97 accurate to date.

Weather station logs, Nome Alaska, February 1987: Recorded aurora borealis displaying in geometric patterns that spell out grocery lists in Sumerian. Lists include items not available until 1994. All items were eventually purchased.

Census data, Constantinople 1453: Population records list 847 residents who cast no shadows. Tax assessments normal, property ownership documented. Imperial survey notes: Citizens appear solid, participate in commerce, pay tithe regularly.
